title: probabilistic-alert-smoothing-eval-gate: add stochastic CI gate to reduce noisy prompt-regression alerts
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: CI has been producing a high volume of transient prompt-regression alerts for low-volume cohorts. These noisy failures increase on-call toil and delay prioritization of true regressions. This change introduces a probabilistic/stochastic gating layer that smooths alerts by estimating a posterior over the cohort regression rate and only opening an incident when the posterior crosses a configurable credibility threshold. Design: - New CI hook `prob-gate` computes a Beta posterior over passed/failed sample counts per cohort, with configurable prior (alpha/beta) and lookback window. - Gate emits three outcomes: allow-fail (treat as transient), gated-fail (record but do not page), and open-incident (page and block merge). - A lightweight failover path triggers a full evaluation run for cohorts that are near-threshold to reduce false positives. - Integrates with existing eval-harness reporters and the CI summary step; metrics emitted for telemetry (posterior_mean, posterior_ci_low, posterior_ci_high, samples_considered). Backwards compatibility: Default configuration preserves current deterministic threshold behavior (alpha=1,beta=1,credibility=0.99) so rollout is opt-in. Configuration is exposed via ci/eval-hooks.yml and via environment variables for Dedicated/Private runs. Implementation notes: - Core logic implemented in eval_harness/hooks/probabilistic_gate.py - CI integration and annotations in ci/hooks/prob-gate.yml - Unit tests in tests/test_probabilistic_gate.py and an integration test fixture using a small synthetic prompt cohort to validate smoothing behavior - Docs in docs/dev/eval-gates.md and example config in examples/ci/prob-gate-example.yaml Checklist: - [x] Core algorithm implemented - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] CI config and annotations - [x] Docs + example config - [x] Telemetry counters and dashboards (PR links included) Impact: This should reduce alert noise for low-sample cohorts while preserving sensitivity for real regressions. Teams can tune alpha/beta/credibility to match risk tolerance. See release notes for how to opt-in and suggested defaults for evaluation suites.
